assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md declares 'Grouping strategy: **by-repository**' and lists two Epics in the Epic Hierarchy table: Epic 1 (TC-9006: trustify-backend, Parent: TC-9006) and Epic 2 (TC-9006: trustify-ui, Parent: TC-9006). Both Epics sit between the Feature and the 8 Tasks as shown in the Task-to-Epic Assignment table.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic Hierarchy table lists Epic 1 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Epic 2 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both follow the '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task-to-Epic Assignment table maps: Tasks 1,2,3,8 (trustify-backend) -> Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-backend'; Tasks 4,5,6,7 (trustify-ui) -> Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md Tasks Created table confirms the same mapping with a 'Parent Epic' column.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 17: '**Incorporates links:** Feature TC-9006 -> Epic 1, Feature TC-9006 -> Epic 2 (Feature links to Epics, not to individual Tasks.)' summary-comment.md line 18-19 confirms: '**Incorporates links:** Feature TC-9006 -> Epic 1, Feature TC-9006 -> Epic 2 (Links are from Feature to Epics. Tasks inherit hierarchy through their Epic parent.)'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Dependencies section shows: Task 1 -> Task 2 -> Task 3 (all backend, sequential numbers 1-3); Task 2 -> Task 4 -> Task 5 -> Task 6 (backend to frontend cross-Epic dependency, backend task 2 has lower number than frontend tasks 4-6); Task 5,6 -> Task 7 (frontend testing). Backend tasks (1,2,3) consistently have lower numbers than their dependent frontend tasks (4,5,6,7). Task 8 (documentation) depends on all.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-test tasks (1,2,4,5,6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing tasks (3: integration-tests, 7: dashboard-tests) contain the required Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (plus bonus Files to Create/Modify/Implementation Notes). Documentation task (8: documentation) contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. No tasks are missing any required sections.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 10: 'A level-1 issue type (Epic) is available.' Epic Hierarchy table shows Parent=TC-9006 for both Epics. summary-comment.md Epic table includes 'Issue Type' column with value 'Epic (level 1)' and Parent=TC-9006 for both Epics.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain a '## Repository' section with a single value: Tasks 1,2,3,8 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4,5,6,7 have 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria' (with checkbox items), and '## Test Requirements' (with checkbox items). Verified across task-1 through task-8.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 digest files exist: task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md. Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex>' format. Examples: task-1-digest.md: 'sha256-md:1c36976c9d29c0caacfcfa2c5d2d9e852cef71eb04c215d8b5b7af0595e598e7'; task-8-digest.md: 'sha256-md:964de9c5c745c26f3fde6a5d31f6a95f66460a9a8225112a8a817904e077dc21'. All hashes are exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed with 'sha256-md:'.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All tasks with Implementation Notes sections (1-7) include conventions with the prescribed rationale format. Examples: Task 1: 'Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/model/summary.rs` matching the convention's `.rs` module structure scope.' Task 4: 'Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's `.ts` API file scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task creates `src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/RemediationDashboardPage.tsx` matching the convention's `.tsx` page component scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations. All rationales follow the 'Applies: task modifies/creates <specific file> matching the convention's <scope>' format, not free-form prose.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md Inherited Field Propagation table: '| **priority** | Major | Yes | Yes | Feature priority is set (not "Undefined"), so it is propagated to all tasks and Epics |'. The additional_fields JSON for both Epics and Tasks includes '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md Inherited Field Propagation table: '| **fixVersions** | RHTPA 1.5.0 | Yes | Yes | Feature has fixVersions set, and `fixVersion scope` in Jira Field Defaults is `both`, so fixVersions are propagated to all tasks and Epics |'. The additional_fields JSON for both Epics and Tasks includes '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. CLAUDE.md confirms 'fixVersion scope: both'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Propagation' section with a table documenting: priority=Major (propagated to tasks and Epics), fixVersions=RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated to tasks and Epics), labels=ai-generated-jira (applied to all). It also includes the full additional_fields JSON showing the exact values applied to Epics and Tasks.
